title: 第8章 柳条

content_zh:
我心想，这他妈到底是谁家的死孩子，还没完了，开一次玩笑也就算了，在这样下去非得闹出人命不可。
我当时就急了，冲二蛋大声吼道：“二蛋，你还想啥呢，赶紧抓住绳子，我拉你回来。”
水里的二蛋听到我声音，扑腾几下，呛了两口水后，赶紧伸手抓住渔网的绳子，我这里使出力气就开始拉他。
不过让我心惊的是，那小女孩的力气贼大，死死的抓住二蛋的小腿不放，我抓住绳子愣是没有拽过她。
一点一点的，我的脚也由岸边踩到了水里，被绳子向水塘深处里拉去，二蛋则是在水里哭喊着，呛了几口水又向水下沉去。
“这死孩子的力气真大，在这么下去救不了二蛋不说，我非得也被她拉下水不可。”我眼看一个人的力气不够，就吼了铁柱一声，叫他过来跟我一起拉。
铁柱显然也发现了事情有些不同寻常，一脸的严肃，连忙跑过来帮我，我二人合力之下，才险之又险的将二蛋拉出水面。
二蛋的脑袋一露出来，就冲我俩哭喊道：“救命啊，有东西拽我腿，我不想死啊。”
我紧忙说二蛋你坚持住，铁柱我俩这就把你给拉上来，我怕两个人力气不够，冲着远处那几个网鱼的孩子喊了几声，把他们也叫过来帮忙一起拉绳子。
铁柱我俩，再加上另外几个孩子，一共六个人，开始合力拉这根绳子。
人多力量大，二蛋终于一点点的被我们向岸边拉扯回来，不过让我背后发凉的是，那个孩子依旧死死的抓住二蛋的小腿不放，并且眼睛恶毒的看向我，就好像跟我有深仇大恨似得。
我当时就急眼了，心想，你这个死孩崽子，给脸不要脸，没完没了是吧，你瞪我干啥，吓唬谁呢，我一来气，倔劲上来了，松开绳子，随手捡起地上的几块小石子，向她劈头盖脸的一顿砸。
我扔出去的小石子砸在了她的身上，她没有躲避，不过看我的眼神更恶毒了，倒是铁柱看到我扔石头，举止非常奇怪，就问道：“你不拉绳子，没事扔石头干嘛啊？。”
我说还不是那个死孩崽子吗，她愣是抓住二蛋的腿不放，我用石头砸她呢，给她点颜色瞧瞧。
铁柱向水里看了看，除了二蛋哭爹喊娘叫救命以外，哪有什么孩子啊，他又问另为几个伙伴，都纷纷摇头说没有看见水里有什么孩子。
听他这么一说，我就有点毛愣了，后背冷汗唰唰直流，为什么我能看见，铁柱他们却瞧不见，在联想到小女孩的恐怖模样和她那惊人的力气，我不禁开始有点怀疑，自己是不是遇上鬼了啊。
这个想法一出现，我就吓得浑身发软，脑袋嗡嗡直响，心口闷得慌，险些喘不过气来，身体随之有些摇摇欲坠起来。
铁柱见我脸色不好看，说你怎么了，没事吧，没事就快来拉绳子，别愣着啊。
我没敢把看到鬼的事儿说给他们几个听，怕吓跑他们，到时候谁来救二蛋，我只好哆哆嗦嗦的抓住绳子，闷不吭声与大伙一同拉，时不时的看了看水底的那个小女孩，心里说不出是什么滋味。
正当我们齐心协力把二蛋拉到一半的时候，出乎大伙意料的是，绳子突然崩的一声，竟然从中间断开了，我们几个顺势一屁股坐在了地上，一时间人仰马翻，哀嚎不绝，非常狼狈。

二蛋眼见绳子断了，顿时吓得面色如土，双手挥舞着，嘴里大喊着救命，又被小女孩向水塘的深处拖去。
这下他们几个可傻眼了，手足无措的不知该怎么办，只有我明白怎么回事，绳子断了，二蛋被鬼带走了，永远回不来了。
那时我才十岁，看着二蛋在我眼前被鬼拖下水，当时既害怕，又委屈，坐在地上哇哇大哭起来，一边哭着，一边大喊救命，小伙伴们听我一喊，愣过神后，也各自扯开嗓子跟着喊起救命来。
也是碰巧，一个扛着锄头的老头正从这里路过，听到我们的叫喊声，扛着锄头就跑了过来。
他向水里看了看，二话不说，折了一根柳树条就跳进了水里，向二蛋那游去。
老头游到二蛋沉下去的地方，在水里摸索一阵，提着二蛋的胳膊，一把将拉出水面。

content_en:
I thought to myself, whose dead child is this? It’s not over yet. It’s just a joke. If this continues, someone will die.
I became anxious at that time and yelled at Erdan: "Erdan, what are you thinking about? Quickly grab the rope and I'll pull you back."
Erdan in the water heard my voice, fluttered a few times, choked a few mouthfuls of water, and quickly reached out to grab the rope of the fishing net. I used all my strength to start pulling him.
But what shocked me was that the little girl was so strong that she held on to Erdan's calf tightly and wouldn't let go. I grabbed the rope but didn't pull her.
Little by little, my feet stepped into the water from the shore, and I was pulled deep into the pond by the rope. Erdan was crying and shouting in the water, took a few sips of water, and then sank into the water.
"This damn kid is so strong. If I keep going like this, I can't save Erdan, and I will have to be dragged into the water by her." Seeing that one person was not strong enough, I yelled at Tiezhu and asked him to come over and pull him with me.
Tie Zhu also obviously noticed that something was a little unusual. With a serious look on his face, he quickly ran over to help me. With the combined efforts of the two of us, we were able to pull Er Dan out of the water with great difficulty.
As soon as Erdan's head came out, he cried to us: "Help, something is tugging on my leg. I don't want to die."
I hurriedly said Erdan, hold on, Tiezhu and I will pull you up right now. I was afraid that the two of us were not strong enough, so I shouted a few times to the children who were fishing in the distance, and called them over to help pull the rope together.
Tie Zhu and we, plus a few other children, a total of six people, began to work together to pull the rope.
With the strength of the crowd, Erdan was finally pulled back to the shore bit by bit by us, but what made my back feel chilly was that the child still held on to Erdan's calf and looked at me with vicious eyes, as if he had a deep hatred for me.
I was anxious at that time, thinking, you damn brat, you are so shameless, you will never stop, right? Why are you glaring at me? Who are you trying to scare? When I got angry, I became stubborn, let go of the rope, picked up a few pebbles on the ground, and smashed her head and face.
The pebbles I threw hit her, but she didn't dodge, but she looked at me more viciously. However, Tie Zhu behaved very strangely when he saw me throwing the pebbles, so he asked, "Why are you throwing pebbles if you don't pull the rope?"
I asked, "Isn't that the dead kid?" She grabbed Erdan's leg and refused to let go. I hit her with a stone to give her some color.
Tie Zhu looked into the water and saw that there were no children except Erdan crying for his father and mother for help. He asked several other friends, and they all shook their heads and said they did not see any children in the water.
Hearing what he said, I was a little stunned, and cold sweat ran down my back. Why could I see it, but Tie Zhu and the others couldn't? When I thought of the little girl's terrifying appearance and her amazing strength, I couldn't help but start to wonder if I had encountered a ghost.
As soon as this idea appeared, I was so frightened that I felt weak all over, my head was buzzing, my heart was so tight, I could hardly breathe, and my body was shaky.
Tie Zhu saw that I looked ugly and said, "What's wrong with you? Are you okay? Come and pull the rope if you're okay. Don't be stunned."
I didn't dare to tell them about the ghost sighting, for fear of scaring them away and asking who would rescue Erdan. I had no choice but to hold on to the rope shivering and pull with everyone in silence. I looked at the little girl under the water from time to time, and I couldn't tell how I felt.
Just when we worked together to pull Erdan halfway, to everyone's surprise, the rope suddenly collapsed and was disconnected from the middle. We sat down on the ground, and for a while we were on our backs, wailing, and very embarrassed.
When Erdan saw that the rope was broken, his face turned pale with fright, he waved his hands and spoke loudly.He shouted for help, but was dragged deeper into the pond by the little girl.
Now they were dumbfounded and at a loss as to what to do. Only I understood what was going on. The rope was broken and Erdan was taken away by the ghost and will never come back.
I was only ten years old at the time. I saw Erdan being dragged into the water by a ghost in front of me. I was scared and aggrieved at the time. I sat on the ground and cried loudly. While crying, I shouted for help. When my friends heard me shouting, they were stunned and started shouting for help at the top of their lungs.
It also happened that an old man carrying a hoe was passing by here. Hearing our shouts, he ran over with a hoe on his shoulder.
He looked into the water, without saying a word, broke off a willow stick, jumped into the water, and swam towards Erdan.
The old man swam to the place where Erdan sank, groped in the water for a while, then took Erdan's arm and pulled him out of the water.
